pr.title: coverage: Make `#[coverage(..)]` apply recursively to nested functions
pr.description:
This PR makes the (currently-unstable) `#[coverage(off)]` and `#[coverage(on)]` attributes apply recursively to all nested functions/closures, instead of just the function they are directly attached to.

Those attributes can now also be applied to modules and to impl/impl-trait blocks, where they have no direct effect, but will be inherited by all enclosed functions/closures/methods that don't override the inherited value.

---

Fixes #126625.
pr.author: Zalathar

issues.title: `#[coverage(..)]` attribute should apply recursively to nested functions/methods/closures

analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, `InstrumentCoverage` eligibility for a local def consulted only attributes attached directly to that def. `#[coverage(off)]` was parsed into `CodegenFnAttrFlags::NO_COVERAGE`, and `is_eligible_for_coverage` checked `tcx.codegen_fn_attrs(def_id).flags.contains(CodegenFnAttrFlags::NO_COVERAGE)`. A parent function/module/impl annotation therefore did not affect any nested function, method, or closure; those nested defs were evaluated independently and remained eligible unless they had their own direct attribute.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation was to decide coverage eligibility only from the current def's direct `#[coverage(..)]`/`NO_COVERAGE` state, without recursively inheriting the nearest enclosing annotation. Thus, for an outer function annotated `#[coverage(off)]`, nested functions and closures were still instrumented and appeared in coverage output, even though the enclosing function was excluded. The corrected behavior resolves `#[coverage(..)]` on the def and recursively through `opt_local_parent` to the crate root: nearest `off` disables coverage, nearest `on` enables it, and no attribute anywhere defaults to enabled.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust programs compiled with `-Cinstrument-coverage` and the unstable `coverage_attribute` feature, containing nested functions/methods/closures and/or functions inside modules and impl/impl-trait blocks annotated with `#[coverage(off)]` or `#[coverage(on)]`. The relevant axis is inheritance of the nearest enclosing coverage attribute, including nested overrides, module nesting, impl methods, closures, and `#[naked]` functions.
analysis.summary: Make `#[coverage(off)]` and `#[coverage(on)]` recursive: coverage eligibility must inherit the nearest coverage attribute from enclosing defs, modules, or impl blocks instead of checking only the function's direct attribute. The fix adds a `coverage_attr_on` query walking `opt_local_parent` and moves naked-function exclusion to an explicit `NAKED` check.
analysis.trigger: A function, method, or closure is nested inside another def, module, or impl block carrying `#[coverage(off)]` or `#[coverage(on)]`, and coverage instrumentation is enabled.
preconditions: The outer enclosing item may be a function, closure, module, impl block, or impl-trait block; the attribute may also be inner (`#![coverage(..)]`).
The nearest enclosing coverage attribute determines the inherited value; a child may override it with its own attribute.
No coverage attribute anywhere up to the crate root means coverage remains enabled by default.
`#[naked]` functions must still be ineligible even after `NO_COVERAGE` is no longer used for direct coverage attributes.
pitfalls: Checking only `codegen_fn_attrs` / direct `NO_COVERAGE` misses inherited attributes on enclosing functions, closures, modules, and impl blocks.
Do not treat any ancestor `off` as unconditional: the nearest attribute wins, so an inner `#[coverage(on)]` can re-enable coverage inside an outer `#[coverage(off)]`.
Attributes on modules and impl/impl-trait blocks have no direct coverage effect themselves; they only provide inherited defaults for enclosed functions/closures/methods.
Removing `CodegenFnAttrFlags::NO_COVERAGE` requires preserving naked-function exclusion via an explicit `CodegenFnAttrFlags::NAKED` check in `is_eligible_for_coverage`.
Malformed coverage values remain a parser/attribute-validation concern; the recursive query assumes other possibilities were rejected by `rustc_parse::validate_attr`.
Recursion must stop at the crate root and default to allowing coverage when no annotation is found.
analysis.testStrategy: Add coverage UI tests using `#![feature(coverage_attribute)]` and `//@ edition: 2021` under `tests/coverage/attr/`, with `.coverage` and `.cov-map` expectations. Cover: outer `#[coverage(off)]` with nested fn/closure/method chains expected to show no counters; inner `#[coverage(on)]` overriding outer `off`; outer `#[coverage(on)]` with inner `#[coverage(off)]`; nested modules with inherited `off`; impl and impl-trait blocks with inherited `off`/`on`; and multi-level closure nesting. Add or retain an `#[naked]` eligibility check regression. Update UI attribute-target tests so modules and impl blocks are accepted while non-function/impl/module targets still produce E0788. Assert coverage-map absence/presence rather than claiming runtime reproduction.
